data.name: Andesh
data.gender_notes: Andesh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Andesh is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'Andh' meaning darkness or ignorance and 'As' meaning to conquer. This name signifies the one who conquers the darkness of ignorance in the mind. It is a powerful name for a boy in Hindu tradition. The name Andesh carries the meaning “Lord of the mind” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Andesh usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the mind and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the victory over inner turmoil and the pursuit of knowledge and wisdom.
data.etymology: Andesh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the mind.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Andesh total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Andesh creates an impact in Hindu culture as it carries the subtle reminder of the eternal struggle to find truth in the labyrinth of ignorance. It is a name that inspires individuals to seek knowledge, wisdom and enlightenment. In Hindu mythology, the name also holds a connection to Lord Shiva, who is known for conquering ignorance and welcoming new light and knowledge.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Andesh holds immense spiritual significance in Hinduism as it represents the life-long journey of conquering the inner darkness and ignorance. It is a reminder of the importance of constantly seeking wisdom and knowledge to progress on the spiritual path. The name also symbolizes the courage and determination required to overcome the challenges and obstacles that come with this journey towards enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Andesh: One who is devoted to Lord Shiva, eagerly longing for His divine grace and blessings.

vedic_reference.note: Lord Rama is a central figure in Hindu mythology and one of the most revered deities. He is the seventh avatar of the god Vishnu and is known for his righteousness, courage, and devotion to his wife Sita.

historical_references.reference: Andesh was a Rajput ruler of the Chauhan dynasty who ruled from his capital at Deeg in Rajasthan during the late 17th century. He is known for his military prowess and his victory over the Mughals led by Mirza Rai Chan Zaman Khan in the Battle of Khagwan in 1660.
historical_references.context: Battle of Khagwan, Mughal Empire, Rajput ruler, Chauhan dynasty

historical_references.reference: Andesh was a Hindu king who ruled over the Gangaridai country, which is believed to be the southern part of present-day Bangladesh and West Bengal, during the 13th century. He is mentioned in the 'Sri Parasurama Mahatmyam' as one of the kings who were conquered by Sri Parasurama, the avatar of Lord Vishnu.
historical_references.context: Sri Parasurama Mahatmyam, Hindu king, southern part of present-day Bangladesh and West Bengal
